quote.author: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard's Almanack (1737)

macro.title: What It Means — VWRA, Bonds, Gold & BTC

reads.label: VWRA (held)
reads.text: still near 52-week highs; equities grind up, but a credibility-shy Fed and firm real yields are a headwind if the "prove-it" mood persists.

reads.label: Global bonds (held)
reads.text: actively bearish — a 30-year at a 2007 high is a real repricing, so the equity–bond hedge is working less well.

reads.label: Gold (read)
reads.text: caught between war-haven demand and higher real yields; net, a deep pullback from January's record even with the war live.

reads.label: Bitcoin (read)
reads.text: trading as a risk asset, not a hedge — soft below resistance in a liquidity-tight tape. The two you hold stay VWRA and global bonds; gold and BTC are read for sensitivity, not endorsed — and BTC's volatility is in a different league.

stories.headline: A Ceasefire Announced Over a Strait Still Shut
stories.dek: Late Saturday, Trump called off the weekend's planned strikes on Iran and said the "perimeters" of a deal were set — the immediate opening of Hormuz, an end to the nuclear threat. By Sunday the strait was still closed, Tehran's hardliners were promising a "decisive response," and eleven US embassies were telling Americans to think about leaving.

stories.headline: The Budget Model That Laps Its Own Flagship
stories.dek: DeepSeek pushed V4-Flash-0731 to general availability on the last day of July — MIT-licensed, free to run, and beating the larger V4-Pro on its own agent benchmarks. It got there not by growing, but by being retrained. And at 13 billion active parameters, it is the first frontier-tier open model in months that plausibly fits on a single home rig.

stories.headline: The Companion in the Glare, Named at Last
stories.dek: For a century, astronomers suspected a second star hid inside Betelgeuse's light. Now a team has imaged it — a candidate at 6.1 sigma — and named it Siwarha, "her bracelet." It is also, they think, doomed: dragged inward, to be swallowed within ten thousand years.

stories.headline: The West Gets Its Line — in the Late 2030s
stories.dek: LTA and SLA have fixed the alignment for Cross Island Line Phase 3: four stations from Jurong Lake District to Gul Circle, up to fifty minutes shaved off a far-western commute. Construction starts in 2027. The trains run "late 2030s." The relief is real; so is the wait.

stories.headline: A Two-Billion-Dollar Bid Into a Cooling Market
stories.dek: The Bayshore Drive site drew a record S$2.128 billion — the first government land parcel outside the CBD ever to clear two billion. It was placed the same fortnight URA's own data showed private prices decelerating and the segment next door falling. Confidence, or a bet against the statistics?

stories.headline: Garmin Built a Screenless Whoop — and Forgot the Subscription
stories.dek: The CIRQA is a fabric band you wear round the clock for sleep, recovery and readiness. It ships at US$199.99, runs ten days on a charge, and — the part that stung the incumbents — works without a monthly fee. Whether it works during intervals is the open question.

stories.headline: Home Assistant Rebuilds the Logbook — and Hands You the Delete Key
stories.dek: The 2026.8 beta turns the old Logbook into a day-grouped "Activity" feed, overhauls the Zigbee device manager, and gathers every IR blaster and RF bridge into one panel. It also ships a single button that can wipe a household's entire event history — and, for anyone mid-migration off Lutron, a reason to wait for the Friday patch.

stories.headline: A Myth You Can Wear, From a Film It Never Appears In
stories.dek: Hamilton and Christopher Nolan built a bronze field watch around The Odyssey — helmet-textured dial, sword-shaped hands, a caseback the director signed. It costs US$1,495, comes in an edition of 2,112, and is the purest object-lesson in the gap between the story and the thing: the watch is set in a Bronze Age that had no watches.

stories.headline: Two Million Dollars Short of History
stories.dek: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" opened to an estimated US$355 million domestic — the second-biggest debut ever, and just US$2 million behind "Avengers: Endgame." Critics gave it a 90; audiences, a 98. The record it missed is what it will chase into its second weekend.

stories.headline: The Bans Arrive; the Parents Aren't Sure They Want Them
stories.dek: More than 35 US states now restrict phones in school, and this summer three of them — Illinois, Indiana, California — moved from law to live classroom. Yet in the same weeks, a survey found nine in ten parents still want their own child reachable during the day. The policy is the word; "techxiety" is what parents feel about the deed.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · Rates & the Regime
stories.headline: A New Fed Chair Talks Tough; the Thirty-Year Says Prove It
stories.dek: Kevin Warsh's Fed held rates on a bruising 9–3 vote — three dissents wanting a hike — and the bond market answered by sending the 30-year to its highest since 2007. Add a surprise MAS tightening and a firm dollar, and the regime writes itself: higher-for-longer, dollar-bid, and a portfolio that has to work with rising real yields.

stories.headline: The Children You Want May Depend on the Friends You Keep
stories.dek: A new fertility report finds that the young adults with the most supportive friendships want, on average, a full extra child compared with the loneliest — a gap that rivals religion. It is a striking correlation. It is also from an advocacy think tank, and measures what people say they want, not what they have.

stories.headline: Thirty Minutes in the Heat Moves Your Whole Immune System
stories.dek: A Finnish study found a single sauna session sends every class of white blood cell surging into the bloodstream — and back to normal within half an hour. It is a vivid finding, widely oversold. The floor of the longevity case, meanwhile, is still the least glamorous thing in the gym: the barbell.

stories.headline: The On-Sales to Set an Alarm For
stories.dek: A heavy Singapore concert autumn, a marquee Grand Prix that becomes a two-race weekend, and a Tokyo calendar tilting into festival season. Two on-sale dates below are worth a reminder — the deed of booking beats the word of "I'll get to it."

stories.headline: The County That Dared to Spend
stories.dek: The Western story about China this year is deflation, cautious consumers, youth who have given up. In the counties — the third-tier towns most correspondents never file from — a different story is running the other way. And in mid-July, China's own press declared it out loud: county spending had "walked out of the sinking-market narrative." When the FT writes this in three weeks, remember where you read it first.
